stem: An asset was purchased for Rs 1,00,000 with a residual value of Rs 10,000 and a useful life of 5 years. The company uses the straight-line method of depreciation. What is the annual depreciation charge and what is the book value at the end of 3 years?

options.text: Annual depreciation Rs 18,000; book value Rs 46,000
Annual depreciation Rs 20,000; book value Rs 40,000
Annual depreciation Rs 18,000; book value Rs 64,000
Annual depreciation Rs 10,000; book value Rs 70,000

per_option_rationale.rationale: SLM annual depreciation = (Cost - Residual) / Life = (100000 - 10000) / 5 = 18000. Book value after 3 years = 100000 - 3 x 18000 = 100000 - 54000 = 46000.
Ignores residual value and depreciates full cost: 100000/5 = 20000 per year; book value = 100000 - 60000 = 40000.
Correctly calculates Rs 18,000 annual depreciation but subtracts only 2 years of depreciation instead of 3: 100000 - 2 x 18000 = 64000.
Uses residual value (10000) as the annual depreciation charge instead of computing (Cost - Residual)/Life; gives book value = 100000 - 3 x 10000 = 70000.

explanation: SLM with residual value: annual depreciation = (cost - salvage) / useful life = (100000 - 10000) / 5 = 18000. After 3 years: accumulated = 54000; book value = 100000 - 54000 = 46000.

explanation_sections.punchline: When a residual (salvage) value exists, SLM depreciates only the depreciable amount (cost minus residual), not the full cost.
explanation_sections.approach: Formula: SLM with salvage. Annual charge = (C - S)/n = (100000-10000)/5 = 18000. Accumulated over 3 years = 54000. Book value = C - accumulated = 100000 - 54000 = 46000.
explanation_sections.lesson: Always subtract residual value before dividing by life in SLM; failing to do so overstates annual depreciation.
explanation_sections.timing: 60 seconds. Trap: depreciating full cost (ignoring residual). Quick check: book value must not fall below Rs 10,000 residual.
